Because the client has irregular cycles and no reliable cycle-based scheduling, the program is non–cycle‑dependent and uses progressive overload, periodized phases, and attention to recovery, insulin sensitivity, and body composition goals commonly important with PCOS. Start date: 2026-06-01. Assume 3–4 sessions/week (I give both 3‑day and 4‑day options). Modify loads to start at RPE 6–7 (or 60–70% 1RM) and progress as listed.

Guiding principles
- Resistance training is first-line: focus on compound lifts, higher weekly volume for lower body and back, plus accessory work for metabolic and strength improvements.
- Progressive overload and variability: 3 phases (Hypertrophy / Strength / Power+Deload).
- Frequency: 3 days/week minimum; 4 days/week option offered for more volume.
- Tempo: when not specified, control eccentric (~2 s), pause 0–1 s, concentric explosive but controlled.
- Rest: compound sets 90–180 s, accessory 60–90 s.
- RPE: aim to leave 1–2 reps in reserve on most sets; last set of main lifts can be RPE 8–9 occasionally.
- Recovery: sleep 7–9 h, prioritize protein intake, manage stress, active recovery on off days.
- Monitoring: track bodyweight, training loads, resting HR, sleep, and subjective energy. Adjust volume if energy very low or training not tolerated.

- Track weekly: bodyweight, sleep, training loads (weights/reps), subjective readiness, any menstrual symptom changes, and any flare episodes.
- Progress load when target reps/sets are completed with good form. Increase 2.5–5% on main lifts or add 1–2 reps as appropriate.
- If performance/energy declines for >1 week, reduce volume by 10–20% and reassess nutrition/sleep/stress.

- A 2‑week return-to-load microplan if she experiences another flare during the programme.
- A one-page pre-session screening checklist for the client.

- This programme maintains the original 12‑week periodised plan but now anchors all flow-day scheduling to May 3, 2026 and applies menstruation-specific lightening on Days 1–5 of each 28‑day cycle.
- Nutrition emphasizes insulin sensitivity while explicitly avoiding under‑fuelling, with targeted iron and anti‑inflammatory support during flow windows.
- Flare-management and lumbar-sparing progressions are integrated and override cycle rules when active.

Cycle context: Early luteal moving to next flow window start Jun 28 (next flow window Jun 28–Jul 2). Expect slightly higher resting temperature and possible early luteal symptoms late week.

Week 9 — 2026‑07‑27 to 08‑02

Additional details and coaching notes

Cardio (integrated across programme)
- Two moderate sessions per week (30–40 min) on non-lifting days or after lifting as a cooldown. Types: incline walking, cycling, rowing or pool. Intensity RPE 5–6. On flow days keep cardio easy (RPE 3–5) and shorter if needed.
- If extra low-intensity activity desired (daily walking 10–30 min), encourage it for insulin sensitivity, mood and circulation.

Nutrition (cycle-aware and anti‑inflammatory; avoids under‑fuelling)
- Calorie strategy: maintain energy to support training. If fat loss desired, keep a modest deficit (-150 to -350 kcal/day) but avoid aggressive deficits. Refeed/maintenance on heavy training/ovulation days recommended.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (spread evenly across meals).
- Carbs: modulate by phase — higher around training and during follicular/ovulation for heavier sessions; moderate in luteal; avoid late-night high-refined carbs if sleep is affected.
- Fats & fibre: 25–35% calories from fat; 25–35 g fibre/day.
- Iron: emphasize iron-rich meals during flow windows (Days 1–5) — lean red meat, legumes, spinach + vitamin C. Consider iron status check with MD if flow heavy.
- Anti‑inflammatory: include oily fish, olive oil, berries, nuts. Consider omega‑3 1–2 g/day if approved by MD. Consider myo‑inositol under clinician guidance for PCOS.
- On flow days: prioritize maintenance calories, slightly higher carbs and iron as needed; avoid under‑feeding which may worsen symptoms.

Flare management integration (if a flare occurs during the 12 weeks)
- Immediate: stop aggravating activities, follow the previously outlined 7–10 day active recovery protocol, refer to physio/MD if needed.
- Replace heavy compound days with modified low-load sessions during flare; do not push through pain.
- Reintroduce load via the staged return‑to‑load template (regress → rebuild → return to intensity), shifting the programme forward by the recovery window length or using lighter Weeks 5–6 before full intensity.

Autoregulation & pre-session checklist (use every session)
- Quick pre-session: sleep hours, energy 1–10, pain score 0–10, flow Y/N (and day), readiness to train Y/N.

- If OK, proceed with planned session; adjust loads by -10–15% if fatigued.

Specific exercise substitutions for lower-back health
- Prefer trap-bar deadlifts and RDLs with controlled eccentric; use goblet/box/front squat instead of heavy back squats when lumbar symptoms present.
- Prioritize unilateral work (split squats, step-ups) and hip thrusts/glute bridges for posterior chain without excessive lumbar flexion/compression.
- Continue daily thoracic mobility and glute activation to reduce lumbar compensation.

Monitoring & progression
- Track weekly: bodyweight, sleep, training loads (weights/reps), subjective readiness, any menstrual symptom changes, and any flare episodes.
- Progress load when target reps/sets are completed with good form. Increase 2.5–5% on main lifts or add 1–2 reps as appropriate.
- If performance/energy declines for >1 week, reduce volume by 10–20% and reassess nutrition/sleep/stress.

Optional add-ons I can provide
- A printable week-by-week calendar with exact dates and session labels (I already used calendar dates above but can give a one‑page grid).
- A 2‑week return-to-load microplan if she experiences another flare during the programme.
- A one-page pre-session screening checklist for the client.
- A 4‑week cycle-aware microcycle template to repeat after week 12.

Summary
- This programme maintains the original 12‑week periodised plan but now anchors all flow-day scheduling to May 3, 2026 and applies menstruation-specific lightening on Days 1–5 of each 28‑day cycle.
- Nutrition emphasizes insulin sensitivity while explicitly avoiding under‑fuelling, with targeted iron and anti‑inflammatory support during flow windows.
- Flare-management and lumbar-sparing progressions are integrated and override cycle rules when active.
